contract.owner_operations: Admitted original connect/catalog/authorization/read/reset/recovery/OAuth operation is owned from first DB request to final delivery. Cancelled caller abandons only its waiter; original operation can complete once. Actual isolated SQLite connect retains DB and session, including cancellation of its caller.
contract.invocation: Cancellation is requested once only during interruptible transport work. Database prepare/delivery, before-send authority check/dispatched commit, cleanup and final result commit remain owned. No second cancellation cuts cleanup; original known call ID is retained. A cancelled before-send read cannot send; committed dispatched intent remains conservatively unknown. A delivered valid response still commits its actual result. Post-response processing failure is unknown, never an assertion of no execution.
contract.session: Failed start/stale/explicit stop/close mark original session retiring before cleanup. False/error retains exact old object, generation and handshake but denies catalog/call/replacement until original close actually succeeds. Health exposes cleanup_pending even if native port omits it. Closing rechecked after lock acquisition and stale cleanup; no late new session.
contract.shutdown: Stop admission then drain original business tasks before transport close. Original transport-close Task survives timeout/cancelled close waiter; active close is reused. Only explicit later close retries an actually completed false/error close. Quiescence includes business tasks, transport pending/busy/starting/retiring and original close receipt, protecting manual action review and instance database release.
contract.unchanged: No new DB schema, protocol timeout reduction, authorization bypass, retry of external writes, model payload disclosure, automatic reconnect or cross-process sharing.
